target_source: fresh measured contact-edge feature propagated by robot state plus historical socket surface; operator-defined bounded contact test

evidence.limitations: Rigid/no-slip propagation unverified. Earlier longitudinal feature discrepancy 24 mm; DO NOT treat predicted point as true connector center. No force sensing or whole-object clearance.

limitations: Unknown clearance; no automatic release; no insertion success assumed.

evidence: The visible card pose is broadly consistent with approaching the motherboard connector region; the images do not establish an obvious obstruction or gross misalignment that rules out this simulator-only trial.
The proposed 2.30 mm cross-edge correction matches the supplied feature-to-historical-socket cross-edge difference.

The propagated feature is 55.33 mm above the historical housing surface. The 57.33 mm vertical advance therefore targets 2 mm below that surface, making this an explicit contact trial rather than a noncontact approach.

A single bounded advance followed by hold and end, without release or automatic search, can provide visual evidence of seating progress, blockage, or displacement. It cannot by itself establish successful insertion.
uncertainty: The current connector interface is occluded; the historical socket view does not establish current clearance.
Rigid/no-slip propagation is unverified, and the predicted feature is not a verified connector center.
The approximately 24 mm along-edge discrepancy remains unresolved and is not treated as a required correction because the selected points may differ.
Whole-object clearance, exact insertion alignment, and contact loads are unknown. Joint and orientation checks do not resolve those uncertainties.
Approval is limited to the stated simulator-only exploratory trial and does not certify safety or success.
